title: Injectivity of the first Cech cohomology map
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let U = {U_i} be an open covering of X. For every sheaf H of O_X-modules, the canonical homomorphism c_H from the first Cech cohomology group of U with values in the underlying abelian sheaf of H to H^1(X,H) is injective; this is the canonical map for the underlying abelian sheaf in the Cech-to-cohomology comparison.

proof.text: Write H_ab for the underlying abelian sheaf of H on the small Zariski site X_Zar. By [lem-sc-zariski-module-abelian-cohomology-agree] there is a canonical isomorphism H^1(X,H) \cong H^1(X_{\rm Zar},H_{ab}), natural in H, between the O_X-module cohomology of [pqf-def-cohomology] and the abelian-sheaf cohomology of [def-sc-zariski-cohomology]. The Cech groups of U with values in H and in H_ab are the same group, since the Cech complex [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] uses only the abelian groups H(U_{i_0\ldots i_p}) and the restriction maps. The canonical map c_H of the statement is the canonical Cech-to-cohomology map c of H_ab followed by this isomorphism, so it suffices to show that c: \check H^1(U,H_{ab}) \to H^1(X_{\rm Zar},H_{ab}) is injective.

Apply [lem-sc-cech-spectral] on the Zariski site to the covering U and the abelian sheaf F=H_ab: there is a convergent spectral sequence E_2^{p,q}=\check H^p(U,\underline H^q(F)) \Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X_{\rm Zar},F), with E_2^{p,q}=0 for p<0 or q<0. Since \underline H^0(F) is the presheaf V \mapsto H^0(V,F)=F(V), E_2^{1,0}=\check H^1(U,F). For r \ge 2 the differential d_r into E_r^{1,0} starts at E_r^{1-r,r-1}=0 (p<0) and d_r out of E_r^{1,0} lands in E_r^{1+r,1-r}=0 (q<0), so E_\infty^{1,0}=E_2^{1,0}. Convergence gives a filtration H^1(X_{\rm Zar},F)=F^0 \supset F^1 \supset F^2=0 (F^2/F^3=E_\infty^{2,-1}=0) with F^1=E_\infty^{1,0}; the edge homomorphism \check H^1(U,F)=E_2^{1,0}=E_\infty^{1,0}=F^1 \subset H^1(X_{\rm Zar},F) is therefore injective, and it is the canonical Cech-to-cohomology map c. With step 1, c_H is injective.
